display.purpose: The SSO device-authorization code only. Nothing else uses this size.

body.purpose: Default running text, list rows, form values.

label.purpose: Uppercase section headings and category markers; also the SSO token badge/expiry text at its plain weight.

mono.purpose: Literal system data a user reads exactly or copies: account IDs, role names, device codes.

caption.purpose: The smallest role: the default-profile badge and the copy-confirmation tooltip.

density-compact.purpose: The Font Size Toggle's own 'S' button label — fixed px, does not scale with the active density.

density-default.purpose: The Font Size Toggle's own 'M' button label — numerically equal to Body but declared as its own fixed step since it belongs to this trio, not the scaling content hierarchy.

density-comfortable.purpose: The Font Size Toggle's own 'L' button label — fixed px, does not scale with the active density.

shadows.name: toast-overlay
shadows.purpose: The single floating overlay in the system. Toast notifications only.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default duration for color/background/border transitions on hover and focus.

motion.name: pulse-danger
motion.purpose: First-click state of the destructive two-click confirm pattern; pulses the icon button's background to demand a second, deliberate click.

motion.name: pulse-connecting
motion.purpose: Opacity pulse on a tunnel's status dot while it is connecting.

terminalPalette.purpose: The Shell page's embedded xterm.js terminal is deliberately excluded from the app's own Editor Blue / status palette because it must faithfully render arbitrary ANSI color codes from whatever CLI runs inside it. It uses the named 'Tokyo Night' 16-color palette instead, set directly in xterm's JS theme object (Terminal.tsx) since it cannot consume CSS custom properties.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one Editor-Blue-filled action per view.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--color-accent, #007acc); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); background: var(--color-accent, #007acc); color: var(--color-on-accent, #ffffff); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, sans-serif; font-size: 0.923rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-accent-hover, #1a8ad4); border-color: var(--color-accent-hover, #1a8ad4); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent-hover, #1a8ad4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: var(--color-accent-active, #0065a9); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border-light, #4a4a4a); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); background: transparent; color: var(--color-text, #cccccc); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, sans-serif; font-size: 0.923rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--color-bg-hover, #333333); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #007acc); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Confirm Icon Button
components.description: First click arms a pulsing danger state instead of a window.confirm() dialog (unsupported in Tauri's webview); a second click on the pulsing icon performs the delete.
components.html: <button class="ds-icon-btn ds-icon-btn-confirm" aria-label="Confirm delete"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M3 6h18"/><path d="M8 6V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h4a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v2"/><path d="M19 6l-1 14a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H8a2 2 0 0 1-2-2L5 6"/><path d="M10 11v6"/><path d="M14 11v6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 28px; height: 28px; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); background: transparent; color: var(--color-muted, #808080); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-icon-btn-confirm { background: rgba(241, 76, 76, 0.25); color: var(--color-danger, #f14c4c); animation: ds-pulse-danger 0.6s ease-in-out infinite alternate; } @keyframes ds-pulse-danger { from { background: rgba(241, 76, 76, 0.15); } to { background: rgba(241, 76, 76, 0.35); } }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard form field: Raised background, border shifts to Editor Blue on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 8px 10px; background: var(--color-bg-tertiary, #2d2d2d); border: 1px solid var(--color-border-light, #4a4a4a); border-radius: var(--radius, 4px); color: var(--color-text-bright, #e8e8e8); font-family: inherit; font-size: 1rem; transition: border-color 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-muted-text, #949494); } .ds-input:focus { border-color: var(--color-accent, #007acc); outline: none; }

components.name: Bordered Card
components.description: The generic Panel-toned, 1px-bordered container used for accounts, profiles, tunnels, and saved configs.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--color-bg-secondary, #252526); border: 1px solid var(--color-border, #3c3c3c); border-radius: var(--radius-lg, 6px); padding: 10px 14px; } .ds-card-title { font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-text-bright, #e8e8e8); font-size: 1rem; } .ds-card-meta { font-family: 'SF Mono', 'Fira Code', monospace; font-size: 0.923rem; color: var(--color-muted-text, #949494); margin-top: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Pill-shaped status indicator; color alone never carries meaning, the label always accompanies it.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-size: 0.846rem; font-weight: 500; padding: 2px 7px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid; } .ds-badge-active { color: var(--color-success, #4ec9b0); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-success, #4ec9b0) 40%, transparent); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-success, #4ec9b0) 12%, transparent); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Active state carries a 2px Editor Blue left border, the system's recurring 'you are here' signature.
components.css: .ds-sidebar-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; width: 100%; padding: 8px 16px; border: none; background: transparent; color: var(--color-muted-text, #949494); font-size: 1rem; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-sidebar-item:hover { background: var(--color-bg-hover, #333333); color: var(--color-text, #cccccc); } .ds-sidebar-item.ds-active { background: var(--color-bg-active, #3c3c3c); color: var(--color-text-bright, #e8e8e8); border-left: 2px solid var(--color-accent, #007acc); padding-left: 14px; }

components.name: Device Code Display
components.description: The system's one Display-scale moment: the SSO device-authorization code, in mono, wide letter-spacing, inside a Raised bordered container.
components.css: .ds-device-code-container { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 20px; background: var(--color-bg-tertiary, #2d2d2d); border: 1px solid var(--color-border-light, #4a4a4a); border-radius: var(--radius-lg, 6px); } .ds-device-code { font-family: 'SF Mono', 'Fira Code', 'Cascadia Code', monospace; font-size: 2.154rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 3px; color: var(--color-text-bright, #e8e8e8); user-select: all; }

narrative.overview:
Charon's own stylesheet names its lineage in a comment: an OpenLens-inspired dark theme. That inheritance runs deeper than the label — the exact hex values for background, accent, and status colors are VS Code Dark+'s own palette. This is not accidental resemblance; it's a deliberate signal to the people who'll use it that this is a tool built by and for engineers who live in an editor and a terminal all day, not a consumer app borrowing dark mode as decoration.

The console is dense by design: a fixed three-region shell (48px top bar, 200px sidebar, 24px status bar) frames a scrollable content area, and nothing in it is built to be spacious. Rows, cards, and badges pack tightly so a screen can hold many accounts, roles, profiles, or tunnels at once. Depth is never faked with shadows — it's built from a strict ladder of background tones, the same technique an editor uses to distinguish gutter from pane from panel. Color is almost entirely absent except where it does real work: one blue for the single primary action per view, and a fixed small set of status colors (teal/amber/red) that mean the same thing everywhere they appear.
keyCharacteristics: Fixed dark theme, VS Code Dark+ derived — no light mode exists.
Base type size is 13px, smaller than typical web defaults, in service of density.
Depth via background-tone layering, not shadows.
One accent color, used sparingly, for the one primary action or piece of live state per context.
Monospace reserved strictly for literal AWS/system data (account IDs, role names, device codes) that users read exactly or copy.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Editor Blue appears on at most one control per view as a filled background — everything else that needs emphasis uses Bright Text or a status color instead. A screen with two blue-filled buttons is a mistake, not a stronger call to action.

rules.name: The Status Trio Rule
rules.body: Success/Warning/Danger are the only three semantic colors in the system, and their meaning never changes: teal is always "good/active", amber is always "in progress/caution", red is always "bad/error/destructive." Never introduce a fourth semantic hue.

rules.name: The Compact Rule
rules.body: The base size is 13px, not the web-typical 16px. Never introduce a component at 16px+ body copy — it will read as foreign against everything around it. The only exception is the Display role.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything a user would copy-paste verbatim (account ID, role name, device code, ARN-like strings) renders in the mono stack. Everything else — including buttons, labels, and status text — stays sans.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest, distinguished only by background tone and a 1px border. A shadow appears only on the one true floating overlay (toasts); introducing shadows on cards, buttons, or hover states breaks the console's visual logic.

rules.name: The Icon/Prose Split Rule
rules.body: Muted Text, Editor Blue, and Danger Red each carry a dedicated "on prose" variant, and the split is load-bearing, not cosmetic: WCAG AA needs only 3:1 for a graphical object (an icon glyph, a status dot) but 4.5:1 for running text, and the base tokens were tuned for the former. Any new text node reaches for the -onprose token; icons, dots, fills, and borders keep the base token. Never use an -onprose variant as a background, border, or icon color, and never render prose in a base token that has an -onprose sibling.

rules.name: The Fixed-Control Rule
rules.body: A control whose job is to set the type scale (the Font Size Toggle) must not itself be styled from that scale — its three preset sizes (10px / 13px / 16px) stay literal px so all three stay visually distinct and stable in every density mode. This is the one intentional exception to "everything scales in rem"; it does not extend to any other component.

dos: Do convey depth with the Void → Panel → Raised → Hover Surface → Active Surface tone ladder, never with a drop shadow (the toast is the sole exception).
Do pair every status dot or colored border with a text label; color alone is never the only signal.
Do render literal AWS/system data (account IDs, role names, device codes) in the mono stack; keep everything else in the system sans stack.
Do use the two-click pulsing .icon-btn-confirm pattern for any destructive action that needs confirmation.
Do keep exactly one Editor-Blue-filled control per view for the primary action.
Do use the -onprose variant (Muted Text on prose / Editor Blue on prose / Danger Red on prose) for any actual text node; reserve the base token for icons, dots, fills, and borders.
Do size ordinary content in rem so it scales with the Font Size Toggle; the toggle's own three preset buttons are the sole, deliberate exception.
donts: Don't call window.confirm(), alert(), or prompt() — Tauri 2's webview does not support them.
Don't add box-shadows to cards, buttons, or hover states — this is a flat, bordered system.
Don't introduce a body text size above 13px (1rem) outside the Display role, or drop below the system's small-label sizes — the scale is deliberately narrow and dense.
Don't add responsive breakpoints or fluid layouts — the shell assumes one fixed desktop window (200px sidebar / 48px top bar / 24px status bar) and has never needed to adapt.
Don't introduce a fourth semantic status color beyond Success Teal / Warning Amber / Danger Red.
Don't render running text in base Muted Text, base Editor Blue, or base Danger Red — none of the three clears 4.5:1 for normal text against Void or Panel; use their -onprose variant instead.

Don't pull the app's Editor Blue / status palette into the terminal's xterm theme, or the terminal's Tokyo Night colors into the app chrome — they're deliberately separate systems for a deliberate technical reason.
